root_cause.text: tpm2_read_public() in the TPM2 sessions subsystem mishandled ownership of the tpm_buf buffer allocated by tpm_buf_init(), omitting required cleanup on the name_size() error path and the normal success return path, which caused a page-allocation memory leak.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds missing tpm_buf_destroy(&buf) before returning when name_size_alg < 0 and again before the final successful return after memcpy(), while the commit message explicitly states that tpm_buf_init() was called but tpm_buf_destroy() was missing on those two exit paths, leaking a page allocation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Free the TPM buffer before returning on invalid name size errors to fix an error-path resource leak.
intent_record.what: The change wraps the `if (name_size_alg < 0)` branch in braces and adds a call to `tpm_buf_destroy(&buf)` before returning `name_size_alg`.
intent_record.how: When `name_size(&buf.data[offset])` returns a negative value, the function now frees the TPM buffer before exiting, preventing the buffer from being left undisposed on this error path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Free the TPM buffer on the successful tpm2_read_public() path to avoid leaking resources.
intent_record.what: A call to tpm_buf_destroy(&buf) was added immediately after memcpy(name, &buf.data[offset], rc) and before returning name_size_alg in tpm2_read_public().
intent_record.how: This ensures the TPM buffer object is cleaned up on this successful return path, preventing the buffer's associated resources from being leaked after copying out the public name data.

grouping_result.intent: Free the TPM buffer on the successful tpm2_read_public() path to avoid leaking resources.

consistency_review.core_intent: Ensure the TPM buffer allocated in tpm2_read_public() is freed on all return paths to prevent resource leaks.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly fix the root cause in tpm2_read_public() by adding missing tpm_buf cleanup on both the name_size() error path and the normal success path, preventing the described memory leak.

candidates.rationale: This early return on the name_size() error path exits without releasing the TPM buffer previously allocated by tpm_buf_init(), directly causing the memory leak.
This normal success-path return occurs after using the buffer but before destroying it, so ownership of the tpm_buf is mishandled and the allocated memory is leaked.

vuln_statements.explanation: This return exits tpm2_read_public() without releasing the tpm_buf previously allocated by tpm_buf_init(). It is the leaking return on the name_size() error path, and the evidence also identifies this same return site as the normal success-path exit that similarly omits buffer cleanup, matching the root cause of mishandled tpm_buf ownership.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function body is sufficient because it includes the full current implementation of `tpm2_read_public()` and all of its return paths. The root cause is a leak of the `struct tpm_buf buf` allocated by `tpm_buf_init()` when cleanup via `tpm_buf_destroy(&buf)` is omitted on certain exits. That vulnerable construct is present here. After `rc = tpm_buf_init(&buf, ...)`, the function has several exits that do not destroy the buffer: (1) `if (name_size_alg < 0) return name_size_alg;` returns directly after `name_size(&buf.data[offset])` without calling `tpm_buf_destroy(&buf)`, and (2) on the normal success path, after `memcpy(name, &buf.data[offset], rc);` it does `return name_size_alg;` without any `tpm_buf_destroy(&buf)`. Those are exactly the missing-cleanup paths described in the root cause. Some error paths do destroy the buffer, e.g. `if (rc) { tpm_buf_destroy(&buf); return tpm_ret_to_err(rc); }`, `if (offset + 4 > tpm_buf_length(&buf)) { tpm_buf_destroy(&buf); return -EIO; }`, `if (rc != name_size_alg) { tpm_buf_destroy(&buf); return -EIO; }`, and `if (offset + rc > tpm_buf_length(&buf)) { tpm_buf_destroy(&buf); return -EIO; }`, but cleanup is still missing on the `name_size_alg < 0` path and on success. Therefore the bug is present and the fix is not yet complete in this commit version.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet includes the full body of the relevant function `tpm2_read_public()` and its helper `tpm2_parse_read_public()`, so it is sufficient to assess the memory-leak issue. In this commit, `tpm2_read_public()` does `rc = tpm_buf_init(&buf, TPM2_ST_NO_SESSIONS, TPM2_CC_READ_PUBLIC);` and on success proceeds to `tpm_buf_append_u32(&buf, handle);`, `rc = tpm_transmit_cmd(chip, &buf, 0, "read public");`, optionally `rc = tpm2_parse_read_public(name, &buf);`, and then unconditionally calls `tpm_buf_destroy(&buf);` before `return rc;`. This unconditional cleanup on the normal path and after the `name_size()`-related parse path means the leak described in the root cause is not present here. The vulnerable construct would be returning without destroying `buf` after `tpm_buf_init()` succeeded, especially on the `name_size()` error path or success path, but that is absent in this code.
